judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's mathematics is right everywhere I checked: log2 8 + log2 4 = log2 32 = 5; ln(8x) = 3ln2 + ln x; 2log3 6 - log3 4 = log3 9 = 2; log6 36 = 2; log2(x/32) = log2 x - 5; log3 4x = log3 20 -> x=5; 3ln2+2ln5 = ln200; log2(x^5/16) = 5log2 x - 4 and 6 at x=4; x/3=7 -> x=21; log48 = 4log2+log3 = 4(0.3010)+0.4771 = 1.6811 -> 1.681; 3lnx - lny - 2lnz = ln(x^3/(y z^2)) with value ln2 at (2,4,1); x^3=27 -> x=3. But the judge's own second bullet cites '3ln x - ln y - 2ln z = ln(x^3/(yz^2))' as VERIFIED, and it is not in verify.json at all - id 11 holds a single eval at x=2,y=4,z=1. The same is true of the other half of problem 8: answer_key.pdf p.2 boxes '5 log2 x - 4' and verify.json id 8 holds only the eval -> 6. So two of the twelve problems have their principal answer - the symbolic rewrite that IS the requested skill on a log-properties fluency sheet - printed unverified, and the Quick Answers bank prints nothing for either part (a). final_response.md defends this with 'A general identity in two positive variables cannot be machine-proved without positivity assumptions the tool does not carry'. That defence is half false and I tested it: verify.py's sym_equal already judges agreement on the points where both sides are REAL (scripts/verify.py, the comment block ending 'log(x) against log(-x) has no such point and stays unequal'), and problem 5 in this very file is a symbolic base-2 equiv that passes. Running the missing 8(a) check, equiv(log(x**5/16)/log(2)) vs 5*log(x)/log(2) - 4, PASSES today. Only the three-variable identity in 11(a) genuinely fails the sampler. A third, smaller finding the judge did not reach: the answer key's Quick Answers bank prints natural logs as common logs - entry 7 reads 'log(200)' for ln 200 and entry 11 reads 'log(2)' for ln 2 - on a sheet that also contains genuine base-10 logs (problems 9, 10), so the bank is ambiguous where the key body is not.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 10 is the item that makes the properties matter: approximate log 48 from log 2 = 0.3010 and log 3 = 0.4771 alone. It forces the factorisation 48 = 2^4 * 3 before any property applies, and it is double-verified - once as log(48)/log(10) and once as the student's own arithmetic 4*0.3010 + 0.4771 - so the printed 1.681 is checked from both ends. The declared trap (multiplying the two logarithms instead of adding) is the exact error the item is built to catch.

Every solution names the property before applying it ('Power property on the coefficient, then the quotient property'), and the three solve items each close by checking the domain condition - problem 6 states 'x = 5 makes both logarithms' arguments positive, so it is not extraneous', and problem 12 states the positivity check on the cube root. The domain habit is taught as part of the method rather than as an afterthought.

The twelve stems avoid a repeated skeleton as the prompt asked: expand, condense, evaluate and solve rotate rather than block, and no two problems share the same base (2, 3, 6, e and 10 all appear), so the change-of-base decision has to be made freshly each time.

root_causes.description: A two-part 'write it symbolically, then evaluate it' problem satisfies the one-check-per-id rule with the part-(b) number alone, so the part-(a) symbolic answer ships boxed but unchecked - on a sheet whose entire topic is the symbolic rewrite.
evidence: answer_key.pdf p.2-3: problem 8 boxes '5 log2 x - 4' then '6'; problem 11 boxes 'ln(x^3/(yz^2))' then 'ln 2'. verify.json ids 8 and 11 each hold exactly one eval entry.
Quick Answers prints '8. 6' and '11. log (2)' - a grader gets no answer at all for either part (a).
final_response.md concedes the gap but attributes it to a tool limitation.

root_causes.description: sym_equal's random sample grid spans negatives, so a multi-variable identity that holds for all POSITIVE values cannot collect enough real-valued agreement points. The author's workaround was to drop the check rather than to bind the identity, and the comment already in scripts/verify.py records that this exact failure mode drove an earlier author to rewrite problems as two-part items.
evidence: Probe against the shipped scripts/verify.py: equiv(log(x**5/16)/log(2)) vs '5*log(x)/log(2) - 4' PASSES; equiv(3*log(x) - log(y) - 2*log(z)) vs 'log(x**3/(y*z**2))' FAILS.

scripts/verify.py comment: 'An author's first draft hit five of them and had to rewrite problems as two-part expand, then evaluate at x = 4 to bind anything at all.' curr-377 problems 8 and 11 are that rewrite.
final_response.md: 'cannot be machine-proved without positivity assumptions the tool does not carry'.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt round-trips the expected string through sympy.sympify/sympy.latex, which collapses ln to \log and expands a base-b logarithm into a change-of-base quotient. The bank therefore prints a different notation from the one the problem asks for and the key body boxes.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: '5. log (x)/log (2) - 5' where the key boxes 'log2 x - 5'; '7. log (200)' where the answer is ln 200; '11. log (2)' where the answer is ln 2.
The same sheet contains real base-10 logs (problems 9, 10), so 'log 200' is not merely unusual notation, it is ambiguous.

improvements.title: Bind the symbolic half of every two-part rewrite-then-evaluate problem
improvements.proposed_change: Require one verify entry per boxed answer and enforce it in tests/check_answer_key.py by failing a problem segment whose box count exceeds its non-manual entry count. For this case add equiv(log(x**5/16)/log(2)) = '5*log(x)/log(2) - 4' under id 8 (verified to pass today) and equiv(3*log(x) - log(y) - 2*log(z)) = 'log(x**3/(y*z**2))' under id 11 once the sampling fix below lands.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: an ak_ problem segment with two \boxed answers and a verify JSON id carrying one non-manual entry. check_answer_key.py must exit 1 and name the unbacked box; it exits 0 before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The requested skill on rewrite-type sheets stops shipping unchecked, and the Quick Answers bank gains the symbolic answer a grader currently has to derive by hand.
improvements.risk: Authors may respond by removing the box rather than adding the check; the failure message should say 'add a check or a manual entry', not 'unbox it'.

improvements.title: Let equiv verify multi-variable identities that hold only on the positive domain
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/verify.py, when either side of an equiv contains log/sqrt/odd-root of a symbol, retry the sample grid restricted to strictly positive values for the free symbols before declaring the vote unmet (the single-variable case already works via the real-valued vote; the failure is that a 3-variable grid rarely lands all three symbols positive at once). Optionally accept an explicit per-entry "assume": "positive" field so the author can state the domain the identity is claimed on.
improvements.regression_test: Add to tests/test_branches.py (or the verify unit suite) an equiv case 3*log(x) - log(y) - 2*log(z) vs log(x**3/(y*z**2)) asserting PASS, plus a negative control log(x) vs log(-x) asserting FAIL. The first currently FAILS - I ran it against the shipped verify.py.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the documented pressure to rewrite log-property problems as two-part evaluate-at-a-number items purely to get something bindable, which is what produced the coverage hole here.
improvements.risk: Restricting the grid could mask a genuine disagreement that only shows up at negative inputs; keep the positive retry as an ADDITIONAL vote after the existing real-valued vote fails, never as a replacement, and keep the negative control in the suite.

improvements.title: Quick Answers must keep the logarithm base and notation the problem asked for
improvements.proposed_change: Stop rendering bank entries by sympifying the expected string blind. Either honour an optional per-entry "display" string that the bank prints verbatim (escaped), or teach _fmt to recognise the change-of-base pattern log(A)/log(b) and print \log_{b}(A), and to print \ln when the entry's expression uses natural log. Same mechanism as the two canonical _fmt defects (relation answers, Python builtins): the bank must not silently renegotiate the form of a verified answer.
improvements.regression_test: Unit test on _fmt/render_entry: expected 'ln(200)' must render as $\ln 200$ (not $\log(200)$) and expected 'log(x)/log(2) - 5' must render as $\log_{2} x - 5$. Both fail today - the shipped bank prints 'log (200)' and 'log (x)/log (2) - 5'.
improvements.expected_impact: On any sheet mixing ln, log10 and log_b - i.e. every logarithm-properties sheet - the grading bank stops being ambiguous about which base an answer is in.
improvements.risk: A display-string escape hatch can drift from the verified value; bind it by requiring that the display string, when sympified, equals the expected value, and fail the build when it does not.

case_summary: Mathematically flawless logarithm-properties practice - I re-derived all twelve answers and every one is correct, the ramp is real, no skeleton repeats, and each solution names the property it uses and checks the domain on the solve items. The defect is coverage plus presentation. Problems 8 and 11 are two-part 'rewrite symbolically, then evaluate'; only the part-(b) numbers are verified, so the boxed 5 log2 x - 4 and ln(x^3/(yz^2)) - the actual skill of the sheet - ship unchecked and are missing from the Quick Answers bank entirely. final_response.md blames a tool limitation, but I ran the missing 8(a) check against the shipped verify.py and it PASSES; only the three-variable identity in 11(a) genuinely defeats the sampler, and that is a fixable sampling gap that verify.py's own comments already flag as having distorted an earlier author's problem design. Third, the bank prints ln as log and base-2 logs as change-of-base quotients, which on a sheet containing real base-10 logs makes 'log 200' actively ambiguous.
